chunks: 3039 - What was narrated by Sayf ibn ʿAmīrah from Manṣūr ibn Ḥāzim, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

I heard him saying: “The sacrifice in Minā is for three days, so whoever wishes to fast must not fast until the three days have passed. And the sacrifice in the towns is one day, so whoever wishes to fast may fast from the next day.”

key_terms.الْأَمْصَارِ: the towns or regional cities outside Minā
key_terms.بِمِنًى: in Minā, the pilgrimage site near Makkah

ai.seo_question: When can a person begin fasting after the days of sacrifice in Minā and in other towns?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on when fasting may begin in relation to the days of sacrifice. It distinguishes between Minā, where the sacrifice period extends for three days, and other towns, where it is limited to one day.
